core_bottleneck.headline: Bronze SynapseNotebook is the single largest contributor to pipeline deviation, with an 80% success rate and extreme runtime variance across runs.
core_bottleneck.description: Bronze SynapseNotebook is the single largest contributor to pipeline deviation, with an 80% success rate and extreme runtime variance across runs. Its duration swings from ~16s (cancelled) to 111s, 126s, 293s, and 341s across observed runs, representing a ~3x spread on successful executions alone. With a -90.99% deviation and 50.7% contribution to total pipeline deviation, this activity is the primary driver of 'Severe' pipeline health.

With a -90.99% deviation and 50.7% contribution to total pipeline deviation, this activity is the primary driver of 'Severe' pipeline health.

runtime_intelligence_agent: GM_Check_File (GetMetadata) exhibits extreme and erratic runtime variance, fluctuating between ~7s and ~94s across runs with a -85.95% deviation and 13.2% contribution to pipeline deviation. Two runs recorded durations of 85-94 seconds for a metadata check that completed in under 9 seconds in other runs. This points to intermittent storage latency or ADLS throttling during file existence checks.

runtime_intelligence_agent: If Condition1 acts as a sequencing bottleneck by wrapping a large downstream execution branch. Its observed durations range from 700s to 769s, accounting for the majority of total pipeline runtime in every successful run. Given that it encapsulates downstream notebook activities (Gold, Generate_Derived_Metrics, Apply_Data_Quality_Rules, Load_Curated_Layer, Post_Load_Validation_Report), its long runtime is primarily inherited from sequential child execution rather than being an independent bottleneck itself. The 6.7% deviation contribution reflects amplification of child activity delays.

runtime_intelligence_agent: The most recent pipeline run (a9c0c8ee) was cancelled after 88.6 seconds, with Bronze cancelled mid-execution. This cancellation is a direct contributor to the pipeline health rating of 'Severe' and the -91.86% pipeline deviation, as the run completed less than 8% of its normal runtime. The cancellation cause is not captured in available telemetry (no error_message), and whether this was user-initiated or system-triggered cannot be determined from the data.

runtime_intelligence_agent: Copy Raw to Bronze exhibits moderate copy throughput deviation (-21.62%, -17.42s) with runtime varying from 60s to 102s across runs. While not a dominant contributor (5.5% of pipeline deviation), the variance is consistent with variable source data volume or network throughput fluctuations rather than a structural pipeline problem. All runs succeeded.

runtime_intelligence_agent: Switch1 and Data Cleaning show positive deviation (running slower than baseline by +11.25% and +11.66% respectively), each contributing 4.1% to total pipeline deviation. Their durations are relatively stable across runs (96-129s for Data Cleaning, 99-129s for Switch1), suggesting a modest but consistent increase in processing time versus historical baseline rather than sporadic spikes. These are secondary contributors.

agent_recommendation_analysis.compilation_adjustment: Enforced explicit schema-on-read, introduced dataframe caching, released cached memory after use, and removed redundant count() scans across 3 activities.

recommendations.title: Align Pipeline Activity Node Size to Notebook Session Configuration
recommendations.description: The pipeline activity definition hard-codes executor_size='Small' and driver_size='Small' (4g memory, 2 vCores), while the Bronze SynapseNotebook session config requests Medium-tier resources (28g driver/executor memory, 4 cores, 2 executors). Update the pipeline JSON activity definition to set executor_size='Medium' and driver_size='Medium' to match the notebook's session configuration. This eliminates the resource mismatch that is forcing fallback behaviour or severe resource contention, which is the most likely root cause of the -90.99% runtime deviation. Validate by comparing Spark UI executor memory allocation before and after the change across at least 5 runs.

recommendations.title: Remove Redundant df.count() Action Following display(df.limit(10))
recommendations.description: The Bronze notebook calls df.count() after display(df.limit(10)), triggering a full CSV scan as an eager Spark action. This is redundant in a production pipeline context and, combined with inferSchema, causes three full passes over the source CSV data. Remove the df.count() call entirely from the production notebook path. If row-count validation is a business requirement, cache the DataFrame before the display call (df.cache()) and then call df.count(), ensuring the data is read only once. Alternatively, defer the count to a post-write validation step using the written output rather than the raw read DataFrame.

recommendations.title: Replace inferSchema with Explicit Schema Definition on CSV Ingestion
recommendations.description: Remove inferSchema=True from the CSV read operation in the Bronze notebook and replace it with an explicitly defined StructType schema. inferSchema requires a full dataset scan before data is processed, effectively doubling I/O cost. Combined with the df.count() call (see separate recommendation), this results in three full passes over the CSV. Define the schema statically based on the known source structure and pass it via the schema= parameter in spark.read.csv(). This eliminates one full dataset scan and reduces job stages. Expected outcome: reduction of at least one Spark job stage and proportional reduction in Bronze notebook runtime.

recommendations.title: Cache DataFrame After Single Read to Eliminate Repeated Full Scans
recommendations.description: After fixing inferSchema and removing df.count(), consolidate all remaining DataFrame actions by calling df.cache() (or df.persist(StorageLevel.MEMORY_AND_DISK)) immediately after the single authoritative spark.read.csv() call with the explicit schema. This ensures that any subsequent actions (transformations, display calls, write operations) reuse the in-memory cached partition rather than re-reading from the CSV source. Pair this with an explicit df.unpersist() at the end of the notebook to release executor memory cleanly. This is particularly important given the Medium node memory allocation (28g) which, once correctly provisioned, provides sufficient headroom for caching the Bronze dataset.

recommendations.title: Implement Notebook-Level Retry Logic with Exponential Backoff and Alerting
recommendations.description: The Bronze SynapseNotebook has an 80% success rate with cancellations observed (16s cancelled run). Add a retry policy at the pipeline activity level: set retryCount=2 and retryIntervalInSeconds=30 on the Bronze notebook activity in the pipeline definition. Additionally, instrument the notebook with structured logging at key checkpoints (session init, schema read, transform, write) and configure a pipeline failure alert via Azure Monitor or Synapse alerts to notify on-call engineers when the Bronze activity exceeds a runtime threshold (e.g., 200s) or fails. This reduces undetected failures and limits the blast radius of cancellations on downstream critical path activities.

recommendations.title: Establish Bronze Notebook SLA Gate to Protect Downstream Critical Path
recommendations.description: Add a pipeline-level timeout on the Bronze SynapseNotebook activity set to 150% of the target healthy duration (e.g., if healthy p50 is ~120s, set timeout to 180s). Combine this with a conditional check activity (If Condition) after Bronze that evaluates activity output status and duration metadata before proceeding to If Condition1, ForEach1, and Switch1. If Bronze exceeds the SLA threshold, route to a failure notification branch rather than propagating delay to all downstream activities. This decouples Bronze instability from downstream orchestration and provides early circuit-breaking behaviour on degraded runs.

target_optimization_forecast.summary: 6 recommendation(s) identified for Data_Pipeline_-_Engineering (synapse). Highest-impact item: 'Align Pipeline Activity Node Size to Notebook Session Configuration' (~97.0% estimated gain, low effort, low risk).

The Small node size in Synapse provides only 4g memory and 2 vCores per node, meaning the session config's memory/core requests cannot be honoured, likely forcing a fallback or causing severe resource contention/queuing that explains the -90.99% deviation.

configuration_agent: Gold and Data Cleaning notebook activities share the same executor_size='Small' / driver_size='Small' activity-level setting vs. their session configs requesting 28g memory and 4 cores per node (2 executors). The same size-vs-session-config mismatch present on Bronze also affects these notebooks, likely contributing to resource pressure on 'synsparkpool' and slower-than-baseline execution.

configuration_agent: All SynapseNotebook activities in the pipeline (Bronze, ForEach Notebook, Data Cleaning, Switch1 Default) share the single pool 'synsparkpool' with no autoscale or num_executors configuration specified at the activity level (num_executors=null, configuration_type=null). Simultaneous or back-to-back Spark sessions from the ForEach (sequential=true) and Switch on the same pool can exhaust pool capacity, causing queuing that cascades into the large negative deviations seen on Bronze (-90.99%) and GM_Check_File (-85.95%), the latter being downstream of a saturated pipeline.

configuration_agent: GM_Check_File (GetMetadata) uses AzureBlobStorageReadSettings (Blob storage) while 'Copy Raw to Bronze' reads from and writes to AzureBlobFSReadSettings/AzureBlobFSWriteSettings (ADLS Gen2). If the file written by the Copy activity lands in ADLS Gen2 but GM_Check_File checks a different Blob Storage endpoint (different dataset 'Dataset' vs. 'adls_source'/'copy_sink'), the check may consistently point at a wrong location, causing retries/waits or unexpected path resolution delay contributing to the -85.95% deviation.

configuration_agent: All activities pipeline-wide have retry=0 with no fallback. For SynapseNotebook activities running on a shared, potentially saturated Spark pool, a single transient cluster startup failure (cold pool) causes immediate activity failure with no retry, which can manifest as anomalously short (failed-fast) durations explaining some of the large negative percentage deviations rather than slow runs.

configuration_agent: Copy Raw to Bronze has no explicit parallelism settings: parallel_copies=null and data_integration_units=null. Without explicit DIU or parallel copy configuration, ADF/Synapse auto-selects conservative defaults. This, combined with the sink writing text with quote_all_text=true and a .txt extension (potentially larger output), may contribute to the -21.62% deviation. Evidence is partial as linked service throughput settings and actual data volumes are absent.

dependency_lineage_agent: GM_Check_File (GetMetadata) exhibits severe and highly variable latency (-85.95% deviation). In two runs it took 85-94 seconds instead of the ~7-8 second baseline seen in healthier runs. This points to intermittent Azure Blob Storage metadata lookup delays or throttling. Although GM_Check_File sits near the tail of the pipeline (after Switch1 and Wait for 10 sec), its spikes directly added 75-85 seconds to overall pipeline duration in runs 73624619 and bc686a21.

dependency_lineage_agent: Copy Raw to Bronze shows a Warning-level deviation (-21.62%) with moderate duration variability across runs (60-102 seconds). As the root node of the entire pipeline critical path, any increase in its duration propagates to every downstream activity including Bronze, If Condition1, ForEach1, and Switch1. Run 73624619 had Copy=102s (highest) and also had Bronze=293s, compounding the upstream delay accumulation.

dependency_lineage_agent: The primary critical path for this pipeline is fully sequential with no parallelism: Copy Raw to Bronze → Bronze → If Condition1 (false branch: Gold → Generate_Derived_Metrics → Apply_Data_Quality_Rules → Load_Curated_Layer → Post_Load_Validation_Report) → ForEach1 (sequential, ForEach Notebook) → Switch1 (Data Cleaning) → Wait for 10 sec → GM_Check_File → IF_File_Exists → Set_File_Found. The total critical path in healthy runs is ~1174-1183s. ForEach1 is configured as sequential (is_sequential=true) with no batch concurrency, meaning notebook iterations cannot parallelize — even though only one notebook is in the default parameter array.

dependency_lineage_agent: Gold notebook and Switch1 (containing Data Cleaning) both show Warning-level deviations (-17.1% and +11.25% respectively). Gold's variability (112-182s across runs) propagates into the If Condition1 total duration since it sits at the head of the false-branch sequential chain. Switch1's +11.25% positive deviation (running longer than baseline) in Data Cleaning (NB02_Data_Cleansing on synsparkpool Small executor) suggests the Spark pool may experience cold-start or resource contention when Switch1 executes after ForEach1 also used synsparkpool.

dependency_lineage_agent: Set_File_Found and IF_File_Exists show Warning-level deviations (-23.91% and -14.21% respectively) despite individually tiny absolute durations (sub-2s). The deviation signal for Set_File_Found is driven by the anomalous run bc686a21 where GM_Check_File took 94s, as IF_File_Exists and Set_File_Found cannot start until GM_Check_File completes. The deviations in these tail activities are therefore inherited symptoms of GM_Check_File's latency spikes rather than independent issues.

dependency_lineage_agent: If Condition1 consistently accounts for 700-769 seconds across all successful runs, making it the single largest time consumer in the pipeline. This is because it executes a sequential chain of up to 6 nested notebooks (Gold → Generate_Derived_Metrics → Apply_Data_Quality_Rules → Load_Curated_Layer → Post_Load_Validation_Report in the false branch, or Silver → Validate → Cleanse → Transform → Enrich → Aggregate in the true branch). The false branch is consistently taken (Amount default=4500 < 5000 threshold) and its chain totals ~545-750s. If Condition1's duration is the primary driver of overall pipeline runtime.

dependency_lineage_agent: GM_Check_File (GetMetadata) exhibits severe and highly variable latency (-85.95% deviation). In two runs it took 85-94 seconds instead of the ~7-8 second baseline seen in healthier runs. This points to intermittent Azure Blob Storage metadata lookup delays or throttling. Although GM_Check_File sits near the tail of the pipeline (after Switch1 and Wait for 10 sec), its spikes directly added 75-85 seconds to overall pipeline duration in runs 73624619 and bc686a21.

dependency_lineage_agent: Copy Raw to Bronze shows a Warning-level deviation (-21.62%) with moderate duration variability across runs (60-102 seconds). As the root node of the entire pipeline critical path, any increase in its duration propagates to every downstream activity including Bronze, If Condition1, ForEach1, and Switch1. Run 73624619 had Copy=102s (highest) and also had Bronze=293s, compounding the upstream delay accumulation.

dependency_lineage_agent: The primary critical path for this pipeline is fully sequential with no parallelism: Copy Raw to Bronze → Bronze → If Condition1 (false branch: Gold → Generate_Derived_Metrics → Apply_Data_Quality_Rules → Load_Curated_Layer → Post_Load_Validation_Report) → ForEach1 (sequential, ForEach Notebook) → Switch1 (Data Cleaning) → Wait for 10 sec → GM_Check_File → IF_File_Exists → Set_File_Found. The total critical path in healthy runs is ~1174-1183s. ForEach1 is configured as sequential (is_sequential=true) with no batch concurrency, meaning notebook iterations cannot parallelize — even though only one notebook is in the default parameter array.

dependency_lineage_agent: Gold notebook and Switch1 (containing Data Cleaning) both show Warning-level deviations (-17.1% and +11.25% respectively). Gold's variability (112-182s across runs) propagates into the If Condition1 total duration since it sits at the head of the false-branch sequential chain. Switch1's +11.25% positive deviation (running longer than baseline) in Data Cleaning (NB02_Data_Cleansing on synsparkpool Small executor) suggests the Spark pool may experience cold-start or resource contention when Switch1 executes after ForEach1 also used synsparkpool.

dependency_lineage_agent: Set_File_Found and IF_File_Exists show Warning-level deviations (-23.91% and -14.21% respectively) despite individually tiny absolute durations (sub-2s). The deviation signal for Set_File_Found is driven by the anomalous run bc686a21 where GM_Check_File took 94s, as IF_File_Exists and Set_File_Found cannot start until GM_Check_File completes. The deviations in these tail activities are therefore inherited symptoms of GM_Check_File's latency spikes rather than independent issues.
